html:
The skull of Sahelanthropus tchadensis, about seven million years old, found in the Djurab desert of northern Chad in July 2001 by Ahounta Djimdoumalbaye, of a team led by the French palaeontologist Michel Brunet.

Nicknamed Toumai, hope of life in the Daza language, it is among the oldest known members of the human line, from near the time humans and chimpanzees split. Its find, 2,500 km west of the East African Rift where most early fossils had come from, showed that early human ancestors lived across a wider Africa. Whether it walked upright is still argued. It lived by a lake when the Sahara was green. See also Lake Chad.
